prompt.brief: Design a low-latency typeahead service that returns relevant, safe, locale-aware suggestions for each prefix while absorbing billions of queries and frequent ranking updates.
successSignals: Define prefix normalization, language/locale, candidate eligibility, popularity/relevance windows, personalization, safety filtering, and ranking versions.
Use compact prefix indexes and hot-prefix caches; explain updates, stale suggestions, long-tail behavior, and memory bounds.
Separate query serving from asynchronous aggregation and index builds, with atomic snapshot publication and rollback.
Explain abuse/privacy filtering, deletion, cache stampedes, regional failover, observability, and a safe fallback.

functional: Accept a prefix, locale, surface, and optional user context; return ranked suggestions with labels, scores, and index freshness.
Ingest query/click feedback, blacklist unsafe or private terms, support popularity windows, and publish versioned index snapshots.
Support tenant or locale isolation, deletion propagation, cache invalidation, replay, and fallback to popular static prefixes.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 suggestion latency under 50ms at the edge and keep index freshness within 15 minutes.
Scale to billions of queries per day with extreme hot-prefix skew without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 5B queries/day, 500k queries/second peak, and millions of indexed phrases
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Low-latency typeahead service commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Low-latency typeahead service writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Low-latency typeahead service version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Low-latency typeahead service by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Low-latency typeahead service work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Low-latency typeahead service projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Low-latency typeahead service projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Low-latency typeahead service records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Low-latency typeahead service latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
